misconception_source.label: Reported the intersection instead of the union

sources.note: independence supports multiplying for the intersection, while a union also includes outcomes in exactly one event

misconception_source.label: Reported the probability that both events do not jointly occur

sources.note: the complement of at least one event is neither event, not the event that A and B do not both occur

misconception_source.label: Added probabilities without subtracting the overlap

sources.note: for unions, P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B); independent events have overlap P(A)P(B)

criteria.required_evidence: For independent events, P(A and B)=(0.36)(0.25)=0.090. P(A or B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A and B)=0.36+0.25-0.090=0.520.

parts.prompt: For members of a large group, the event that a member joins a study group has probability 0.36, and the event that a member attends a review session has probability 0.25. The two events are independent. What is the probability that a randomly selected member has at least one of these two events occur?
